data.title: Biotech Dealmaker: Sanofi’s $41B Insmed Buyout Anchors Holiday Week As Lilly Continues Buying Spree
data.description:
Key points:
  • Paris-based Sanofi (SNY) announced earlier this week an agreement to acquire rare disease drugmaker Insmed (INSM) for $175 per share in cash, equating to roughly $41 billion in equity value.
  • AbbVie’s acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics for approximately $10.9 billion, announced in June, was the largest pure biopharma company deal of 2026 before Sanofi-Insmed.
  • American drugmaker Eli Lilly ( LLY), known for its obesity drug franchise, agreed this week to acquire UK-based and privately held LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million in cash, continuing its purchasing frenzy.

Deal activity in biotech was selective this week but featured outsized transactions, anchored by Sanofi’s acquisition of Insmed, the largest deal in the sector for 2026, while Eli Lilly extended its buying streak.

Sanofi Agrees To Buy Insmed for $41 Billion

Paris-based Sanofi (SNY) announced earlier this week an agreement to acquire rare disease drugmaker Insmed (INSM) for $175 per share in cash, equating to roughly $41 billion in equity value. The price represented about a 46% premium to Insmed’s unaffected closing price on November 18 and roughly 17% above the prior day’s close.

The deal brings two commercial respiratory medicines under Sanofi—Brinsupri (brensocatib), the first approved therapy for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and Arikayce—plus the late-stage candidate treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP).

Sanofi said the transaction strengthens its immunology and rare-disease respiratory franchise as it prepares for future pressure for its blockbuster Regeneron-partnered drug Dupixent and is expected to be accretive to business earnings by the end of 2028. Closing is anticipated in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.

AbbVie’s acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics for approximately $10.9 billion, announced in June, was the largest pure biopharma company deal of 2026 before Sanofi-Insmed. Earlier this year, Sanofi completed the acquisition of Dynavax Technologies for about $2.2 billion in a bid to add the latter’s adult hepatitis B vaccine HEPLISAV-B to its portfolio and strengthen its adult immunization lineup.

Lilly Acquires Preclinical Huntington’s Developer LoQus23

American drugmaker Eli Lilly ( LLY), known for its obesity drug franchise, agreed this week to acquire UK-based and privately held LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million in cash. The amount includes an undisclosed upfront payment plus development and regulatory milestones.

LoQus23’s lead asset, LQT-23, is a preclinical drug expected to treat Huntington’s disease. The company expects to submit a clinical-trial application by year-end.

Eli Lilly has been the most active large-pharma acquirer in 2026, announcing roughly 11–12 company acquisitions with total potential value, including milestones, exceeding $25–32 billion, and spanning sectors across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, vaccines, and rare diseases as it seeks to diversify its offerings and portfolio. Earlier this month, the company announced that it would buy Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion. In March, the company announced it would buy Centessa Pharmaceuticals for up to $7.8 billion.

How Did SNY And LLY Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SNY jumped from 'bullish' to 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while retail chatter rose from 'high' to 'extremely high' levels.

Meanwhile, sentiment around LLY jumped from 'bearish' to 'bullish' levels, accompanied by 'normal' message volume.

While SNY has added 10% year-to-date, LLY has added 30%.

data.title: Zero To Sixty: Tesla Cybercab Fleet Tops 1,000 In Texas, Lucid Starts Fully Driverless Tests And Chinese EV Maker Posts Stronger Margins
data.description:
Key points:
  • Texas Department of Motor Vehicles data now lists 1,107 Cybercabs, bringing the state’s total robotaxi vehicles to 1,841.
  • Nuro, Lucid and Uber began fully driverless public-road testing of Lucid Gravity robotaxis in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale this week. 
  • On Rivian, Seaport Research initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and $18 target, highlighting the R2’s volume potential and autonomy options and terming it its top EV pick.

The Thanksgiving holiday week was relatively quiet for EV makers, but Tesla added more Cybercabs to its Texas roster in one day this week, lifting the total above 1,000. Rival Lucid began fully driverless Gravity testing with Nuro and Uber, and U.S.-listed Chinese makers reported earnings and expansion plans.

Tesla Scales Cybercab Fleet And Dallas Service

Texas Department of Motor Vehicles data now lists 1,107 Cybercabs, bringing the state’s total robotaxi vehicles to 1,841, with roughly 60% Cybercabs and remaining Model Ys.

Cybercabs, Tesla’s dedicated robotaxi offering with two seats and no steering wheels or pedals, operate in Austin and Dallas. The company launched services in Dallas last week after months of operating it purely in Austin.

Lucid, Nuro And Uber Start Driverless Bay Area Testing

Rival Lucid Motors, meanwhile, is moving towards the robotaxi market itself. Nuro, Lucid and Uber began fully driverless public-road testing of Lucid Gravity robotaxis in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale this week. Employee rides are next, the company said.

The commercial launch, earlier aimed at late 2026, is now expected in the first quarter of 2027 in the Bay Area, with Houston later. Uber has committed to buying at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles fitted with the Nuro Driver technology for its own fleet.

Analyst Names Rivian A Top Pick

On Rivian, Seaport Research initiated coverage with a Buy rating and $18 target, highlighting the R2’s volume potential and autonomy options and terming it its top EV pick.

“Smart design choices (traditional SUV shape), RIVN’s strong software and tech leadership, expanding brand awareness and strong backlog will support meaningful delivery upside in 2027,” the firm said about the R2, as reported by EV.com.

The R2 is Rivian’s latest offering, priced lower than its other models. The company started deliveries of the vehicle in June with its higher-end variant, and hopes to add cheaper variants next year. The lowest-priced variant is expected to be priced around $45,000, close to Tesla’s bestselling Model Y. The company expects the vehicle will scale volumes and drive it towards profitability.

Chinese EV Maker Updates

Chinese EV maker Li Auto, meanwhile, reported third-quarter revenue of RMB 28.8 billion ($4.32 billion), up 5.4% year over year, on 99,964 deliveries. The company’s net loss narrowed to about RMB 310 million, gross margin recovered to 16.7 percent, and free cash flow turned positive at RMB 1.96 billion. Fourth-quarter guidance is 110,000–115,000 deliveries, compared to the 109,194 vehicles it actually delivered in Q4 2025.

At the Guangzhou Auto Show, Li Auto’s rival XPeng outlines its expansion plans outside China. The company now plans five new overseas models in 2027, and aims to more than double overseas sales next year after topping 100,000 this year, and targets international robotaxi and IRON humanoid-robot deployments later in 2027.

NIO’s more affordable Firefly brand, meanwhile, reached 100,000 cumulative deliveries about 19 months after its start and expects November volume to exceed 10,000 for the first time. Firefly, Nio and Onvo brands cumulatively.

All the stocks clocked considerable gains this week. Overall, TSLA clocked 16% gains, marking its best week since May 2025. RIVN clocked 18% gains, marking its best week since July, while LI clocked its best week since March 2024 with 18% gains, while NIO added 16% and XPEV 15%. LCID was the sole player to clock single-digit gains.

Exchange Rate: $1= RMB 0.15

data.title: JPMorgan Plans a Private Club for Well-Heeled Clients in a 1930s Branch — WSJ
data.description:
By Ben Glickman

A block off Central Park, JPMorgan Chase is turning a 1930s three-story brick building into a new offering for its richest clients: an exclusive Upper East Side club.

JPMorgan has been renovating the mansion-like structure at the corner of Madison Avenue and East 64th Street — built as an elaborate bank branch by its predecessor, Bank of Manhattan — for more than a year to allow it to serve food and drink. Public filings show audacious plans to turn the space into something akin to a members club, complete with lounges and a dining room, kitchen and bar.

The space is likely to be used as a venue to host clients of its private bank, which provides white-glove service to its highest-end customers, people familiar with the matter said. To be a private-bank client at JPMorgan, a client needs at least $10 million in investable assets.

The exact programming for the space is still being determined, a spokesman said.

The endeavor, code-named Project Ruby, is the latest effort by JPMorgan to bolster its luxe spaces and services for wealthy clients.

The bank added to its wealth-management business locations when it acquired failed bank First Republic and upgraded many of its branches into JPMorgan-branded locations, complete with additional amenities like private offices and libraries. They are a step up from its Chase brand, which is the biggest consumer bank in the country.

JPMorgan Chase has been building airport lounges, acquired travel services to plan vacations and added new offerings for its well-to-do clients, including connecting them with vendors for anything from private jets to valuing art.

These ultrawealthy customers are at the center of a fight in the banking world in recent years. The banks earn significant fees for managing their fortunes, but are fighting to take on their entire financial lives: offering advice to their estates and to their businesses.

Surging stocks since the pandemic and explosive-artificial intelligence investments have left a large and growing pie of wealth held by the top 0.1% of Americans. Blockbuster initial public offerings of long-private companies, notably SpaceX and Anthropic, have minted millionaires overnight. A generation of baby boomers is both figuring out how to spend their wealth and how to pass it down.

Other wealth managers and credit-card companies have launched similar high-end services, and some have built clubs for clients. But an expansive private-event space would be a new arrow in JPMorgan's quiver for the ultrawealthy.

The neo-Georgian building was completed in 1933 at the height of the Great Depression as a branch for Bank of the Manhattan Trust Company, which would eventually merge into Chase and then JPMorgan. In recent years it has served as an old-fashioned Chase branch for modern-day JPMorgan Chase, complete with ATMs.

It is in an elite neighborhood, standing a few steps from a window display featuring paisley leather handbags of Italian luxury fashion house Etro; the Beretta Gallery, which prominently displays hunting jackets but none of its firearms; and De Beers diamond necklaces.

The bank expects costs for the project to be about $19 million, according to an analysis of city filings by The Wall Street Journal. Records show the bank is installing a new heating, ventilation and air conditioning system, plus an elevator and two dumbwaiters for kitchen service — all part of a near gut renovation of the historic structure.

Some details of Project Ruby were earlier reported by the lifestyle newsletter run by Carson Griffith, called "Rich People Sh — ."

Documents filed with the city show that JPMorgan's project is far from complete. Work on installing piping, drains and bathroom and kitchen fixtures appears to be ongoing, according to work permits filed earlier this month.

On a recent day, small crews were installing drywall in the building, with the entire structure draped in a tarp meant to re-create the building's facade. An open door to the site on Madison Avenue showed wires still hanging from the ceiling and dumpsters holding construction materials.

Renovating an old bank branch comes with its own complications. Last year, crews spent months disassembling the old branch's metal vault, piece by piece, said Paolo Alavian, owner of Altesi, an Italian restaurant next door.

Write to Ben Glickman at ben.glickman@wsj.com

data.title: US Fintech Weekly: Payment Networks Rally Into Black Friday As Wedbush Backs Brokerages
data.description:
Key points:
  • Mastercard and Visa posted strong weekly recoveries as Black Friday sales kicked off. 
  • Wedbush initiated coverage of Robinhood and Coinbase with ‘Outperform’ ratings. 
  • There were no legal updates during the holiday-shortened week. 

Domestic card networks and merchant payment processors staged a broad-based rally during the Thanksgiving-shortened trading week ending November 27, buoyed by Black Friday consumer spending expectations and steady cross-border settlement metrics.

Moreover, with most of the quarterly earnings updates out of the way and a resurgence seen in tech stocks this week, investor attention would now move to the Federal Reserve’s policy decision due in December to judge the future course of capital allocation.

Traders fully price in two Fed rate hikes by March and point to nearly a 90% chance of a third increase by mid-2027, compared to expectations two weeks earlier for three hikes by September and a 35% chance of a fourth, as per the CME FedWatch tool.

U.S. shoppers are increasingly leaning on AI tools to compare models, evaluate specifications, and weigh alternatives before visiting a retailer's website or store, according to Adobe's 2026 holiday shopping data.

According to Adobe’s holiday sales trends report for 2026, stronger digital demand is propelling overall e-commerce growth this season. Marta Frattini, the global retail and consumer strategy lead at Adobe, said in a LinkedIn post that the company projects online Black Friday sales will reach $12.9 billion, up 9.2% from a year earlier, followed by an expected $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday—a projected single-day record spend as per Adobe.

Infrastructure Shifts Across Mastercard, Visa And PayPal

Mastercard (MA): Mastercard shares climbed 6.86% over the week to close Friday’s shortened session, supported by strong payment volumes and spending amid the ongoing Holiday season. The stock rebounded from losses arising from last week’s third-party vendor cyber incident. On November 19, 2026, Mastercard disclosed a cyberattack involving a third-party service provider that exposed limited email addresses for a small subset of cardholders.

Visa (V) and PayPal (PYPL): Visa gained 6.89% for the week to recoup all of its mid-November losses, while PayPal stock added about 11% for the week.

Most payment stocks also gained after Wedbush initiated coverage on Mastercard and Visa with an ‘outperform’ rating.

Wedbush Initiates Coverage On Robinhood And Coinbase 

Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD): Robinhood shares jumped 9.25% for the week after investor sentiment was bolstered earlier this week when Wedbush analyst Moshe Katri initiated coverage of Robinhood with an ‘Outperform’ rating, citing strong user monetization and expansion in alternative trading products.

Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN): Coinbase shares gained about 5% this week. While Goldman Sachs trimmed its price target from $210 to $181 on November 24, Wedbush launched coverage with an ‘Outperform’ rating on November 25, highlighting long-term growth drivers beyond spot crypto volatility.

Federal Rules And Legal Updates

There were no major federal and legal updates pertaining to fintech players for the week ending November 27.

data.title: Citigroup's $35 Billion Bookkeeping Snafu Sparks Shake-Up in Upper Ranks — WSJ
data.description:
By Alexander Saeedy, Ben Dummett and Joe Wallace

A $35 billion bookkeeping blunder in Citigroup's London hub has sparked an internal shake-up and undermined efforts by America's most error-prone big bank to repair its relationship with regulators around the world.

The bank over the summer injected approximately $3 billion into a major U.K. subsidiary after an employee revealed it had been undercounting a key measure of its balance sheet, said a spokeswoman, who described the error as an "internal capital modeling issue."

The mistake shaved $35 billion off the unit's "risk-weighted assets," which regulators use to determine how much loss-absorbing capital banks need to hold. The broker-dealer subsidiary is one of Citi's biggest and most important outside the U.S.

Citi is now scrambling to limit the damage. At least two managing directors who had oversight of financial reports to regulators are no longer in their positions as of this fall, people familiar with the matter said. The bank declined to comment on their departure.

The bank's chief risk officer, Zdenek Turek, recently moved to London from New York and is working to correct the reporting issues, some of the people said.

Tiina Lee, Citi's chief executive in the U.K., said she was stepping down in October. Some of the people said her departure was unconnected to the reporting problem, but her exit adds to the turbulence in Citi's large London operation.

The Citi spokeswoman said Turek's move to London was planned before the problem came to light and was therefore unrelated, adding that the subsidiary never fell below minimum capital levels required by regulators.

The mistake is a setback for CEO Jane Fraser's attempt to draw a line under Citi's long history of unforced errors, some of which contributed to the ouster of her predecessor. The bank is still working to fix internal controls after a slapdown by U.S. regulators in 2020. That year, Citi accidentally paid $900 million to creditors of a cosmetic company.

In 2022, a Citi trader sparked a brief crash in European stocks by entering a preposterously large number in a trading system, and in 2024, U.S. regulators fined the bank $136 million for failing to make progress on cleaning up its act.

Citi has discussed the accounting problem at its U.K.-based unit with officials from the Federal Reserve, which supervises the global parent company, people familiar with the matter said. The spokeswoman declined to comment on conversations with regulators.

The problem for Citi concerns the use of proprietary financial models to calculate "risk-weighted assets," a measure that requires banks to hold more capital against assets — such as complex derivatives — that are riskier than others, such as government bonds. Some banks are allowed to use their own models to determine how much risk they have taken and the requisite capital they should hold to protect from losses.

While the U.K. regulator had given Citi the go-ahead to use some of their own proprietary models, the bank applied them beyond the scope of that approval.

The spokeswoman said the Bank of England hadn't given the green light for a Europe-based desk to use the internal models, which deployed them nonetheless.

The models undercounted Citi's actual risk-taking by around $35 billion, or around 20% of all the reported risk-weighted assets at Citigroup's U.K. subsidiary. The U.K. unit reported it had around $150 billion in risk-weighted assets last year, according to corporate filings.

Calculating risk-weighted assets is inherently complex, so errors aren't unusual. But Citi's mistake stands out for its magnitude, according to one of the people familiar with the matter.

The problem came to light after an employee rang the alarm. The bank then "quickly commenced an internal investigation and escalated this issue to regulators," the Citi spokeswoman said.

The parent company had the funds available to send capital to London and didn't have to sell stock or borrow to do so, the spokeswoman said.

A U.K. regulatory filing shows that at the start of November, Manjira Sen-Gosain, Citigroup's chief risk officer for its U.K. unit, left her position. Her LinkedIn page has been taken down.

Sen-Gosain couldn't be reached for comment.

Banks require approval from the Bank of England, which regulates banks in the U.K., before being allowed to use their own internal models to calculate risk-weighted assets. Persuading the central bank can be arduous — particularly if the model is going to be applied to a significant part of the bank's business. Risk-weighted asset models can permit significant reductions in capital requirements.

Once they are in use, the models typically have some element of self-testing. Bank of England supervisors often keep a close eye on how they are performing to make sure banks aren't undercounting, according to people familiar with the process.

It isn't uncommon for the Bank of England to approve models for certain defined purposes. Going beyond the limits of the approval can be seen as a big problem by the regulator, though how serious depends on the size of the ultimate mistake.

data.title: US Black Friday online sales to cross $13 billion, Adobe says
data.description:
US shoppers to spend above $13 billion online on Black Friday, according to Adobe Analytics data, as bargain-hunting consumers look past inflation and high gas prices.

Online spending on Black Friday reached $9.7 billion through 6:30 p.m. ET (2330 GMT), up 12.8% from last year, according to Adobe. The final total is expected to land between $13 billion and $13.4 billion.

  • Spending is projected to remain strong over the weekend. Saturday spending is expected at $6.1 billion, up 6% from last year, and Sunday spending is forecast at $6.4 billion, up 7.5%

  • Cyber Monday is forecast to remain the season's biggest online shopping day, driving $15.1 billion in spending, up 6.2% from last year

  • Across the five-day stretch from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, online spending is projected to rise 7.4% to $47.5 billion

  • Separate data from Salesforce showed Black Friday online sales generated $5.9 billion in the US and $30.7 billion globally in the first half of the day, keeping it on track for projected spending of $18.7 billion in the US, a 4% growth year over year, and a 5.2% rise to $83 billion worldwide

  • Adobe, which in September forecast Black Friday online sales would rise 9.2% to $12.9 billion, expects US holiday online spending this year to grow at a similar pace to last year's

data.description:
GUADALAJARA, Mexico, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the “Company” or “GAP”) announces that the Initial Public Offering (“IPO”) of FIBRA GAP was successfully completed yesterday.

The offering was carried out under the ticker symbol “FGAP26” through the issuance of 391,004,247 Energy and Infrastructure Investment Trust Certificates (“CBFEs”) at a price of Ps. 20.00 per certificate, for a total amount of Ps. 7,820.1 million. The offering included participation from Pension Fund Administrators (“Afores”) and the general investing public.

The proceeds from the offering will be used to subscribe for shares representing the capital stock of the concession-holding companies for the twelve Mexican airports, as well as to cover issuance expenses. Once these expenses have been deducted, FIBRA GAP will make the corresponding capital contributions, acquiring a 3.98% equity stake in each of these companies. These funds will help finance the investments committed for 2027 under the 2025–2029 Master Development Program.

With this issuance, GAP diversifies its sources of financing and strengthens its capacity to continue executing its investment program, which is focused on the expansion and modernization of airport infrastructure in Mexico.

For all matters related to FIBRA GAP, please contact Gisela Murillo via email at gmurillo@aeropuertosgap.com.mx.

Company Description

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) operates 12 airports throughout Mexico’s Pacific region, including the major cities of Guadalajara and Tijuana, the four tourist destinations of Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos, La Paz and Manzanillo, and six other mid-sized cities: Hermosillo, Guanajuato, Morelia, Aguascalientes, Mexicali, and Los Mochis. In February 2006, GAP’s shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “PAC” and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “GAP”. In October 2018, GAP entered into a concession agreement for the Norman Manley International Airport operation in Kingston, Jamaica, and took control of the operation in October 2019.

data.title: The Weekly Spread: What Shaped US Treasury Yields And The Dollar This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • As U.S. stock indices ended higher at the end of the week, staging a strong post-Thanksgiving holiday comeback, investors pulled away from safe-haven assets.
  • The Dollar Spot Index edged up 0.2% on the week and rose 1.9% in November, putting it on pace for a third consecutive monthly advance and its longest weekly winning streak since January 2025. 
  • Traders have fully priced in two Federal Reserve rate hikes by March and nearly a 90% probability of a third by mid-2027. 

U.S. Treasury prices slipped as trading resumed following the Thanksgiving holiday during the week ending November 27, 2026, as a recovery in equities reduced appetite for safe-haven fixed income.

Yields rose across maturities by six to eight basis points in an abbreviated Friday session, bringing the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield to 4.93% near session highs. With tech shares finding footing late in the week, fixed-income markets adjusted to a renewed push-and-pull between equity risk appetite and safe-haven demand.

While yields rose across the curve on Friday, on a weekly basis, only shorter-duration yields saw a significant uptick, while longer-duration bonds, the 10-year and 30-year, were almost flat on a weekly basis.

The spread between the U.S. 10-year yield and the U.S. 2-year yield ticked lower to its lowest since February, down by seven points to 0.22% in the week ending November 27, showing growing market bets for a hawkish Federal Reserve.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF (TLT) ticked marginally higher by 0.2% during the whole week, while the shorter-duration iShares 1-3 year ETF (SHY) was flat.

Retail sentiment on TLT and SHY was ‘bullish,’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

Asset / Benchmark Close (November 27) Weekly Change 
U.S. Dollar Index 104.01 +0.2%
U.S. 2-Year Treasury Yield 4.72% +7 bps 
U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield 4.94%Flat 
U.S. 30-Year Treasury Yield 5.33%Flat
U.S. 10Y2Y Yield Spread Flattening curve-

For several weeks running, the momentum in U.S. tech and artificial intelligence equities has served as a central driver for sovereign debt markets, with surging equity valuations consistently dampening appetite for fixed-income assets and vice versa.

Yield Curve & Global Sovereign Markets 

The yield curve, which is the difference between the yields of longer and shorter-term maturities, flattened this week, down seven basis points, mostly on account of a faster spike in the 2-year yield.

Generally, a spike in lower duration yields signals a hawkish expectation from the Federal Reserve. For instance, traders fully price in two Fed rate hikes by March and point to nearly a 90% chance of a third increase by mid-2027, compared to expectations two weeks earlier for three hikes by September and a 35% chance of a fourth, as per the CME FedWatch tool.

The U.S. dollar edged higher on Friday and gained 0.2% for the week, extending its longest weekly winning streak since January 2025 while rising 1.9% in November toward a third consecutive monthly gain—its strongest monthly run since late 2024.

The greenback strengthened against most developed market peers, including the Japanese yen and Swiss franc, supported by safe-haven demand after a sharp equity selloff briefly pushed the Nasdaq 100 into bear-market territory earlier this week.

data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Allied Critical Metals Inc. (OTCQB: ACMIF) (FSE: 0VJ0) ("Allied" or the "Company") announced today the release of its unaudited consolidated financial statements for the first quarter of 2026, together with its Management Discussion and Analysis (the "Financial Disclosures"). The Financial Disclosures will be posted on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. All values in the Financial Disclosures are in United States dollars unless otherwise stated.

The Company is also pleased to announce the appointment of John Chou as its new Chief Financial Officer. John Chou is a senior finance executive with more than 25 years of experience in financial management, corporate finance, accounting, taxation and public-company reporting. He has held senior finance leadership positions across the natural resources, energy and consumer sectors. Mr. Chou previously served as Vice-President of Finance at Gran Colombia Gold Corp. (now Aris Mining Corporation), where he was involved in the financial management of a publicly traded gold mining company with significant operations in Colombia. Prior to that, he served as Vice-President of Finance at Frontera Energy Corp., a publicly listed South American oil and gas company, where he gained extensive experience in the financial management of an international resource business. Earlier in his career, Mr. Chou held financial and accounting positions with Deloitte, where he developed a strong foundation in financial reporting, assurance and taxation. Mr. Chou is a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA, CA), holds an MBA from the Schulich School of Business at York University and a Bachelor of Commerce degree from the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management.

Roy Bonnell, Chief Executive Officer of Allied Critical Metals, commented, "We are very pleased to welcome John to the Company as Chief Financial Officer. John brings a wealth of experience in public-company finance, with an impressive track record in the resource sector, including senior finance roles at Gran Colombia Gold and Frontera Energy. His experience managing financial operations, reporting and corporate finance at publicly traded resource companies will be invaluable as we advance our projects and execute on our growth strategy. We look forward to working with John as we enter this next phase of the Company's development."

The Company would also like to thank Sean Choi for his contributions and commitment during his tenure as Chief Financial Officer and wishes him every success in his future endeavours. Sean will assist with an orderly transition to ensure continuity in the Company's financial reporting and operations.

About Allied Critical Metals Inc.

Allied Critical Metals Inc. is a Canadian-based mining company focused on the advancement and revitalization of its 100%-owned Borralha Tungsten Project and the Vila Verde Tungsten Project in northern Portugal.

The Borralha Project is one of the largest undeveloped tungsten resources globally and benefits from a favourable Environmental Impact Declaration (DIA), positioning the Project for advancement toward feasibility and development. Vila Verde represents additional exploration upside within the same strategic jurisdiction. In October 2026, the Borralha Project was selected as a Strategic Project under the European Union's Critical Raw Materials Act, the only Portuguese project and the only tungsten extraction project included in the European Commission's latest selection.

Tungsten has been designated a critical raw material by the United States and the European Union due to its strategic importance in defense, aerospace, manufacturing, automotive, electronics and energy applications. Currently, China, Russia and North Korea account for approximately 87% of global tungsten supply and reserves, highlighting the importance of secure western sources.

Further details regarding the Borralha Project are available in the Company's current preliminary economic assessment technical report prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 entitled "NI 43-101 Technical Report Preliminary Economic Assessment, Borralha Tungsten Project, Parish of Salto, District of Vila Real, Portugal", dated effective April 14, 2026, which is published on the Company's website at www.alliedcritical.com and under its profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

data.title: Alerian MLP ETF Tax Update
data.description:
Alerian MLP ETF (the “Fund” or “AMLP”) has modified the estimate of the Fund’s deferred tax liability and recorded a tax accrual adjustment of approximately $(2.8) million (approximately $0.012 per share) into the net asset value (NAV) of the Fund on November 30, 2026. As part of the tax accrual adjustment, the Fund’s deferred tax liability (DTL) has decreased primarily due to updated tax reporting and other tax related modifications that are routine for the Fund's tax analysis. The Fund will rely to a large extent on information provided by the MLPs, which is largely reported on a delayed basis and is not necessarily timely, to estimate deferred tax liability for purposes of financial statement reporting and determining the NAV. From time to time, the Adviser will modify the estimates or assumptions regarding the Fund’s deferred tax liability as new information becomes available and may consider, among other matters, the duration of statutory carryforward periods, shareholder transactions, underlying index constituent changes and market conditions. The Fund’s estimates regarding its deferred tax liability are made in good faith; however, the daily estimate of the Fund’s deferred tax liability used to calculate the Fund’s NAV could vary significantly from the Fund’s actual tax liability.

ALPS Portfolio Solutions Distributor, Inc. is also the distributor for the Alerian Energy Infrastructure ETF and the ALPS | Alerian Energy Infrastructure Portfolio. Please direct any inquiries to info@alerianmlp.com or by calling 1-866-759-5679.

Important Disclosures

An investor should consider the investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses carefully before investing. To obtain a prospectus containing this and other information, call 1-866-759-5679 or visit www.alpsfunds.com. Read the prospectus carefully before investing.

Shares of ETFs are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemable.

All investments are subject to risks, including the loss of money and the possible loss of the entire principal amount invested. Additional information regarding the risks of this investment is available in the prospectus.

Investments in securities of Master Limited Partnerships (MLPs) involve risks that differ from an investment in common stock. MLPs are controlled by their general partners, which generally have conflicts of interest and limited fiduciary duties to the MLP, which may permit the general partner to favor its own interests over the MLPs.

A portion of the benefits you are expected to derive from the Fund’s investment in MLPs depends largely on the MLPs being treated as partnerships for federal income tax purposes. As a partnership, an MLP has no federal income tax liability at the entity level. Therefore, treatment of one or more MLPs as a corporation for federal income tax purposes could affect the Fund’s ability to meet its investment objective and would reduce the amount of cash available to pay or distribute to you. Legislative, judicial, or administrative changes and differing interpretations, possibly on a retroactive basis, could negatively impact the value of an investment in MLPs and therefore the value of your investment in the Fund.

The Fund invests primarily in a particular sector and could experience greater volatility than a fund investing in a broader range of industries.

Investments in the energy infrastructure sector are subject to: reduced volumes of natural gas or other energy commodities available for transporting, processing or storing; changes in the regulatory environment; extreme weather and; rising interest rates which could result in a higher cost of capital and drive investors into other investment opportunities.

All K-1s are received and processed by the Alerian MLP ETF. The Alerian MLP ETF distributes a single Form 1099 to its shareholders. This notice is provided to you for informational purposes only and should not be considered tax advice. Please consult your tax advisor for further assistance.

If, due to tax law changes or for other reasons, an MLP in the portfolio is deemed to be taxable as a corporation rather than a partnership for federal income purposes, then income would be subject to federal income taxation at the MLP level. This would reduce the amount of cash available for distribution to the fund which could result in a reduction of the fund’s value. The Fund is taxed as a regular corporation for federal income purposes, which reduces the net asset value of fund shares by the accrual of any deferred tax liabilities. Depending on the taxes paid by the fund as a result of income and/or gains from investments and/or the sale of MLP interests, the return on an investment in the Fund will be reduced. This differs from most investment companies, which elect to be treated as “regulated investment companies” to avoid paying entity level income taxes. The ETF is taxed as a regular corporation and is subject to US federal income tax on taxable income at the corporate tax rate (currently as high as 21%) as well as state and local taxes.

The Fund is classified for federal income tax purposes as a taxable regular corporation or so-called Subchapter “C” corporation. As a “C” corporation, the Fund accrues deferred tax liability for its future tax liability associated with the capital appreciation of its investments and the distributions received by the Fund on equity securities of master limited partnerships considered to be a return of capital and for any net operating gains. The Fund’s accrued deferred tax liability, if any, is reflected each day in the Fund’s net asset value per share. The deferred income tax expense/(benefit) represents an estimate of the Fund’s potential tax expense/(benefit) if it were to recognize the unrealized gains/(losses) in the portfolio. An estimate of deferred income tax expense/(benefit) is dependent upon the Fund’s net investment income/(loss) and realized and unrealized gains/(losses) on investments and such expenses may vary greatly from year to year and from day to day depending on the nature of the Fund’s investments, the performance of those investments and general market conditions. Therefore, any estimate of deferred income tax expense/(benefit) cannot be reliably predicted from year to year.

The Fund employs a “passive management” - or indexing - investment approach and seeks investment results that correspond (before fees and expenses) generally to the performance of its underlying index. Unlike many investment companies, the Fund is not “actively” managed. Therefore, it would not necessarily sell or buy a security unless that security is removed from or added to the underlying index, respectively.

ALPS Advisors, Inc., registered investment adviser with the SEC, is the investment adviser to the Fund. ALPS Advisors, Inc., ALPS Distributors, Inc. and ALPS Portfolio Solutions Distributor, Inc., affiliated entities, are unaffiliated with VettaFi and the Alerian Index Series.

data.title: UraniumX Announces Flow-Through Private Placement
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / UraniumX Discovery Corp. (the "Company" or "UraniumX") is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement of up to 36,363,636 flow-through shares at a price of $0.055 per FT Share for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $2,000,000 (each a "FT Share") (the "Offering"). No warrants will be issued to subscribers in connection with the Offering. The Company may increase the size of the Offering to accommodate additional demand.

The FT Shares will qualify as "flow-through shares" within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the sale of FT Shares to incur eligible" Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" within the meaning of subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (Canada), which will be renounced to the subscribers in an amount not less than the subscription price of the FT Shares, with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026 and to incur such expenses on or before December 31, 2027.

Proceeds will fund the Company's ongoing exploration activities at Murphy Lake.

Closing of the Offering is subject to receipt of all necessary corporate and regulatory approvals, including the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange. All securities issued under the Offering will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

The Company may pay finder's fees to eligible persons in connection with the Offering, in accordance with the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

About UraniumX Discovery Corp.

UraniumX Discovery Corp. is a Canadian-based junior uranium exploration company focused on advancing uranium properties in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, one of Canada's most active uranium districts. The Company's flagship Murphy Lake Uranium Property is located in the northeastern Athabasca Basin, where UraniumX is earning up to a 70% interest through an option agreement with F4 Uranium Corp. UraniumX additionally holds 100% interests in the Zoo Bay and NeoCore uranium properties, and is advancing a project generator approach across its broader portfolio by optioning non-core assets while retaining royalties and equity, allowing the Company to concentrate exploration capital on Murphy Lake.

On Behalf of UraniumX Discovery Corp.

Esen Boldkhuu, CEO

This news release contains "forward looking information" and "forward looking statements" within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities laws (collectively, "forward looking statements"). All statements, other than statements of historical fact, included herein are forward looking statements. Forward looking statements in this release include, but are not limited to, statements regarding the Offering, the renunciation of exploration expenses, and the Company's future plans, objectives, and exploration activities.

Forward looking statements are based on reasonable assumptions, estimates, and opinions of management as of the date hereof and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such forward looking statements. These factors include, but are not limited to, the Company's inability to complete the Offering on the terms described herein or at all, fluctuations in market conditions, volatility in equity and capital markets, risks inherent in mineral exploration and development, environmental risks, reliance on key personnel, regulatory approvals, and changes in laws and regulations.
